comparison: Both evaluate the same claims (C3, C33-C36, C42-C46, C70) about PN calcium responses predicting odor preference. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with statistically significant correlations after Bonferroni correction. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, acknowledging 'solid evidence' but noting correlations are 'statistically significant but relatively weak,' indicating acceptance with reservations about strength.

Both evaluate identical claims (C31-C32, C38-C39) about ORN responses not predicting odor-vs.-odor preference. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the negative result is well-supported with appropriate outlier analysis. Peer reviewers implicitly accept by noting the study identifies peripheral locus without challenging ORN findings.

Partial overlap on Brp-behavior correlation claims. OpenEval (C4, C53-C57, C75-C76) rates SUPPORTED despite non-significant test set. Peer review (C4, C55-C60, C75-C77) rates UNCERTAIN, noting correlations are 'statistically significant but relatively weak.' Peer review includes additional claims about Brp as partial explanation (C58-C60, C77) that OpenEval addresses separately in R4.

OpenEval R4 evaluates claims (C58-C60, C77-C78) comparing Brp vs. calcium predictive power as SUPPORTED. These claims partially overlap with peer R3 which rates Brp findings UNCERTAIN due to weak correlations. OpenEval emphasizes the comparison is appropriate; peer reviewers accept significance but question strength.

Strong overlap on modeling claims. OpenEval R5 (C6, C61-C65, C67-C69, C79, C81-C82) rates comprehensive modeling SUPPORTED. Peer R4 (C6-C7, C64-C65, C67-C69, C81-C82) also rates SUPPORTED, explicitly praising modeling efforts as 'mechanistically ground observed data correlations.' Both agree modeling successfully validates main conclusions.

Both address modeling negative controls. OpenEval R6 (C7, C66) rates SUPPORTED for controls identifying non-responsible variation sources. Peer R12 (C62-C63, C66) also rates SUPPORTED, praising modeling controls. Minimal overlap (C66) but both affirm value of negative/positive controls in modeling.

Partial overlap on model validation. OpenEval R5 includes model validation claims (C61, C79) as part of comprehensive modeling evaluation (SUPPORTED). Peer R11 separately evaluates just validation claims (C61, C79) as SUPPORTED, noting 'data analyses are sophisticated and appropriate.'

Both address idiosyncrasy differences between PNs and ORNs. OpenEval R7 (C28-C30) rates SUPPORTED for increased PN idiosyncrasy. Peer R6 (C26-C30) also rates SUPPORTED, accepting that PNs are more idiosyncratic, consistent with ORN-PN synapse as variation locus. Peer review includes broader characterization claims (C26-C27).

Perfect agreement on yoked control experiment. Both evaluate identical claims (C47-C48) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes this rules out experience as confound. Peer reviewers implicitly accept by not challenging this control, strengthening interpretation that calcium predicts preference.

Perfect agreement on temporal dynamics. Both evaluate identical claims (C49-C52) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes alignment between behavior prediction and odor decoding. Peer reviewers accept without challenge, consistent with main conclusions about neural idiosyncrasies driving behavior.

Partial overlap on behavioral stability. OpenEval R10 (C25-C27) rates SUPPORTED for behavioral stability and dual nature of responses. Peer R10 evaluates only behavioral stability (C25) as SUPPORTED. Both agree stability validates correlating neural measures with behavior.

OpenEval R10 includes claims about stereotyped and idiosyncratic responses (C26-C27) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R6 also addresses these claims as part of broader variability characterization (C26-C30), rated SUPPORTED. Both accept this dual nature of responses.

Perfect agreement on PCA organization. Both evaluate identical claims (C40-C41) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this reveals organizational structure of variation. Peer reviewers accept without challenge, noting consistency with praised modeling work and identification of key glomeruli.

Different evaluations of noise-corrected correlation estimate. OpenEval rates C37 as UNCERTAIN due to very wide confidence interval (0.06-0.90). Peer review rates same claim SUPPORTED, not challenging the statistical inference approach. Both acknowledge it provides context without changing main interpretation.

Perfect agreement on main integrative conclusions. Both evaluate identical claims (C5, C71-C73) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergent evidence from functional, structural, and computational approaches. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'solid evidence for at least one locus of individuality,' though noting correlations are relatively weak.

Perfect agreement on model limitation. Both evaluate C80 as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this acknowledges limitation while providing reasonable explanations without undermining main conclusions. Peer reviewers accept this limitation as consistent with overall modeling acceptance.

Partial overlap on Brp density observations. OpenEval R3 includes basic Brp observations (C53-C54) as part of broader Brp-behavior correlation evaluation (SUPPORTED). Peer R14 separately evaluates just these basic observations (C53-C54) as SUPPORTED without challenge.

Perfect agreement on background context. Both evaluate identical claims (C1-C2, C8-C10) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are well-supported by literature and appropriately frame research. Peer reviewers affirm study addresses 'core problem in behavioral neuroscience.'

Perfect agreement on anatomical background. Both evaluate identical claims (C11-C14) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these represent accurate background knowledge. Peer reviewers accept without challenge as necessary context for interpreting findings.

Perfect agreement on prior work summary. Both evaluate identical claims (C15-C24) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes all claims supported by appropriate citations. Peer reviewers accept without challenge as establishing foundation for current investigation.

Different evaluations of speculative claims. OpenEval rates C74, C86-C88 as UNCERTAIN, noting they are largely speculative with limited direct experimental support. Peer review rates overlapping set (C74, C78, C83-C88) as SUPPORTED, accepting these as appropriately framed possibilities typical of discussion sections.

OpenEval R15 evaluates experimental conditions and genetic context (C83-C85) as SUPPORTED, ruling out genetic variation as major contributor. Peer R19 includes these claims in broader speculative discussion evaluation, also rated SUPPORTED as appropriately framed possibilities.

Minimal overlap on modeling negative controls. OpenEval R6 includes C7 (negative control) as part of modeling controls evaluation (SUPPORTED). Peer R4 also includes C7 in broader modeling praise (SUPPORTED). Both affirm value of systematic testing approach.

Minimal overlap on modeling controls. OpenEval R5 includes C62-C63 (negative/positive controls) in comprehensive modeling evaluation (SUPPORTED). Peer R12 separately evaluates these controls (SUPPORTED), praising them as strengthening ORN-PN synapse conclusion.
